Subject: Technical deep-dive recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Samira,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really useful conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Pain points you called out:
- P1: High tail-latency on personalized search ranking during peak traffic (black-friday style spikes).
- P2: Cost unpredictability when models are scaled naively for peak concurrency.
- P3: Data isolation and auditability requirements for user signals (S3 retention + audit logs).

Goals we heard:
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 120ms for reranking requests (50-150 tokens).
- Throughput: sustain 2k qps during marketing promotions, with bursts to 6k qps for 30 min windows.
- Desired pilot window: 6 weeks with a canary to 10% of traffic, then ramp.

Immediate next steps:
1) Share your SLO/traffic spreadsheet (you mentioned an export) — you can upload to the Drive link or reply with the file.
2) Alex/Samira: decision on whether pilot needs to run in us-east-1 or inside your GCP VPC (impacts private deployment).
3) We'll schedule a technical deep-dive w/ our infra leads to align on topology and model sizing (proposed: Monday 3/9 at 10am PT).

I've attached a short template to capture SLOs and traffic shapes and included an initial architecture diagram we discussed.

Attachments: acme_slo_requirements.xlsx (template), redwood_arch_diagram_v2.pdf

Thanks — I’ll loop in the infra folks in the follow-up.

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the concise recap. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- SLOs: 95p <120ms is correct. We also want P99 < 400ms if possible for SLA reporting.
- Traffic shape: baseline 1.2k qps, predictable peaks to 2-3k for promotions, and rare bursts up to 6k for 20-40 minute windows.
- Model: currently using a finetuned reranker (BERT-large variant) in-house; open to trying a quantized OPT/LLama-style candidate for cost testing as long as ranking quality holds.

We uploaded our SLO/traffic export to the Drive link you shared and added comments to the spreadsheet. Regarding deployment: we'd prefer private deployment in our GCP project (VPC peering) for the pilot if Redwood supports it — security wants traffic to stay in our VPC.

Holding Monday 3/9 10am PT for the deep-dive; will invite our infra lead (Samira) and the ML lead (Ishan).

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap and next steps — deployment topology & sizing (notes)

Marissa / team / Acme,

Below are initial notes for the deep-dive. These are engineering-level estimates — we'll validate during the session and adjust to observed latency profiles.

Summary of proposed topology (Private deployment with Redwood control plane + customer VPC peering):
- Control plane (Redwood-managed) sits in Redwood account; inference nodes deployed into a dedicated GCP project inside Acme's VPC via peered VPC networks/Shared VPC.
- Dedicated GPU pool (NVIDIA A10G or A100 depending on cost/availability) provisioned in the customer's project; autoscaling constrained to preserve burst capacity semantics.
- Ingress: requests flow over private peering; egress logs sent to customer-owned BigQuery/S3 for audit.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a smaller quantized variant in-case of capacity pressure (canary policy).

Model requirements & sizing (rough):
- Current: finetuned BERT-large (approx 340M-420M params depending on variant). If this is actually BERT-large (340M), expected token-latency profile at 16-bit (FP16) on A10G:
  - 50 tokens: median ~35–45ms, 95p ~90–120ms, P99 ~300–380ms depending on KV cache hit rate.
  - QPS per GPU (FP16, batched): ~400–800 qps (batched workloads, continuous batching).
- Quantized int8 variant (8-bit):
  - 50 tokens: median ~25–35ms, 95p ~70–110ms, P99 ~220–320ms.
  - QPS per GPU (int8): ~600–1200 qps.
- Recommendation: for their target 2k sustained qps, start with 2–3 x A10G GPUs in dedicated pool for the quantized path; keep a small FP16 pool (1–2 GPUs) as a fallback/quality path. This gives headroom for bursts when combined with autoscaling + prefix caching.

Caching & batching considerations:
- Enable prefix/KV cache for reranker to cut token compute on repeated contexts. Cache hit rate assumptions will significantly affect P99.
- Continuous batching with a 8–12ms latency floor yields better throughput; configure dynamic batch sizing to meet 95p SLO.

Operational notes / SLO guardrails:
- Aim to meet 95p <120ms in the quantized path; track P99 regressions and auto-fallback to FP16 when we detect quality or latency violations.
- Instrument per-route latency and token-level costs. Push logs to Acme's BigQuery for audit/retention.

Attachments referenced: redwood_arch_diagram_v2.pdf (updated), mutual_action_plan.docx

I'll present these slides and a quick cost/throughput spreadsheet on Monday.

—Dev Patel
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
